ablations: None -- single-variable follow-up. The detector is held at D3 (relmax); the ONLY change vs EXP-FP-0126 D3 is the progress guard.
background: EXP-FP-0126 killed H1 cleanly: the adaptive detector (D3) fixed the 0120 misfire mechanically (the 0.98 grid_world goal tick now flags terminal=True), but learned goals stayed below frozen on 4/4 seeds. Mechanism (verified by gain-history inspection, seed 88101): the single terminal tick cap-set branch_credit=north (first branch winner) AND progress_credit=north (canonical tie-break -- zero shaping receipts that episode). Final gains {north: 2.0, rest 1.0}: the agent became a north-attractor with no unlearning path (non-goal ticks on grid_world are negative/zero and change no gains), bumping into the north wall; learned totals more negative than frozen on 3/4 seeds. The open question: is the ARBITRARY PROGRESS PIN the harmful half, or is the lock-in concept itself mismatched to navigation?
baseline: frozen = same class (D3 + guard), frozen=True, gains pinned 1.0, paired per seed.
bit_identity_check: delayed_reward seeds 88201/88202 (reused -- code-equivalence check, not a new measurement): D3+guard learned totals must be bit-identical to EXP-FP-0126 D3 learned totals (the guard can never trigger where shaping receipts are nonzero; reaching the corridor end requires >=10 forward moves, each earning shaping).
conditions: grid_world v1.0.0, 8 eps x <=100 steps, branch_channels = all movement channels, GoalCountingAdapter; arch_a WorkspaceTick, neutral specialists, capacity=4, gain_lr=0.15, theta=0.45, gain_cap=2.0. Detector D3 (FLOOR=0.1, REL=0.5) + progress_guard=True. attention_ecr_detector.py extended additively; canonical files untouched. Fresh seeds {88301,88302,88303,88304} (zero prior use at sealing).

frozen_gates.G0: canonical files byte-identical pre/post: attention_ecr_repro.py, attention.py, tick.py, grid_world.py, delayed_reward.py, k5_multitask_generalization.py
frozen_gates.G1: fabrication-tripwire CLEAN on new code, pre-run
frozen_gates.G2: determinism spot-check: first-seed learned arm recomputed, 1e-12, else VOID
frozen_gates.G3: hash-chained receipt via experiments/harness.py write_receipt + verify_chain

guard_design: New kwarg progress_guard=True on AdaptiveTerminalECR. In _absorb_success: if sum(ledger.shaping_receipts.values()) == 0 (no shaping evidence this episode), skip the progress cap-set (progress_credit=None, recorded) and lock in the branch choice only. The detector classification, shaping path, pre-branch demotion, truncation, and clamping are untouched.
honest_prior: The branch pin alone may suffice to recreate the attractor (on 88101 the first-branch winner was ALSO north), in which case the harm persists and the verdict is that the lock-in concept -- not just the tie-break -- is mismatched to navigation. A no-harm outcome implicates the tie-break specifically. Both are clean, informative, and preregistered.
hypothesis: H1: disarming the arbitrary progress cap-set (branch-only lock-in when the episode contains zero shaping receipts) removes the harm measured in EXP-FP-0126: on grid_world, D3+guard learned gains show no arbitrary-channel pinning, and learned is no longer worse than frozen.
limitations: 4 seeds; neutral specialists; a no-harm gate is weaker than a win gate -- this experiment characterizes which half of the lock-in carries the harm, it does not promise ECR wins on navigation.
null: H0: the harm persists under the guard (learned goals < frozen goals on >=1 seed) -- the branch pin alone recreates the attractor, and the lock-in is inherently mismatched to navigation tasks.
preregistered_metric: grid_world: goal_episodes(learned) vs goal_episodes(frozen) per seed; NO-HARM iff learned >= frozen (not strict) on 4/4 fresh seeds {88301,88302,88303,88304}. Secondary (mechanism): final learned gains must show no cap-set channel other than a first-branch winner (progress_credit=None recorded on every terminal tick).
title: Progress-tie-break guard: which half of the ECR lock-in harms navigation? (EXP-FP-0126 follow-up)

verdict_mapping.harm_removed_4_4: H1 SUPPORTED -- the progress tie-break is the harmful half; the guard is INTEGRATED as a required companion to any adaptive detector
verdict_mapping.harm_persists: H0 -- clean characterization: the lock-in concept is mismatched to navigation (every move is a branch; pinning any single direction at cap builds an attractor). Recorded as the bound; no further follow-up in this lane
